summary: 文章从长期缺觉和睡眠障碍切入，说明睡眠不足会影响判断，并依次梳理非快速眼动睡眠与快速眼动睡眠的特征和可能功能。研究者指出，人类仍未充分理解睡眠各阶段，因此不能轻易用药物或短时补觉代替正常睡眠。

paragraphs.brief: 根据美国疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 的数据，超过8000万美国成年人慢性睡眠不足，这意味着他们睡眠时间低于每晚建议的最低7小时。
sentences: According to the United States (U.S.) Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), more than 80 million American adults are chronically sleep deprived, meaning they sleep less than the recommended minimum of seven hours a night.
根据美国疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 的数据，超过8000万美国成年人慢性睡眠不足，这意味着他们睡眠时间低于每晚建议的最低7小时。
The resulting fatigue contributes to more than a million auto accidents each year, as well as to a significant number of medical errors.
由此造成的疲劳导致每年发生100多万次汽车事故，并造成大量医疗错误。
Even small adjustments in sleep can be problematic.
即使是小的睡眠调整也会有问题。

On the Monday after a daylight-saving time change in the U.S.—when the clocks are moved ahead one hour—there is a 24 percent increase in heart attacks and a jump in fatal car crashes, compared with other Mondays.
周一，在美国的日光节省时间后，当时钟向前移动一个小时，与其他星期一相比，心脏病发作率增加了24%，致命的车祸率上升了。

paragraphs.brief: 大约三分之一的美国人在一生中至少会患有一种公认的睡眠障碍。
sentences: During their lifetimes, about a third of Americans will suffer from at least one of the recognized sleep disorders.
大约三分之一的美国人在一生中至少会患有一种公认的睡眠障碍。
They range from common sleep disorders to much rarer and stranger conditions such as sleep apnea and restless leg syndrome.
它们从常见的睡眠紊乱到更罕见和陌生的条件，如睡眠敏化和不动的腿综合症。
For example, in exploding head syndrome, booming noises seem to reverberate in your brain as you try to sleep.
比如说，在爆炸头综合症中，振动的噪音似乎在你的大脑里回响，当你试图睡觉的时候。
Also, people with Kleine-Levin syndrome will, every few years, sleep nearly nonstop for a week or two.
而且，患有克莱因-列文综合症的人每隔几年会几乎一两个星期不眠不休地睡觉。
However, insomnia is by far the most prevalent of these problems and the main reason 4 percent of U.S. adults take sleeping pills in any given month.
然而，失眠是这些问题中最普遍的问题，主要原因是4%的美国成年人在任何月份服用安眠药。

paragraphs.brief: 演进使我们睡眠灵活，时间灵活，容易受到干扰，因此可以把注意力引向更高的优先事项。
sentences: Evolution endowed us with sleep that is flexible in its timing and easily disturbed, so that attention can be directed to higher priorities.
演进使我们睡眠灵活，时间灵活，容易受到干扰，因此可以把注意力引向更高的优先事项。
The brain has an automatic override system that can wake us in all stages of sleep when it perceives an emergency like the cry of a child.
大脑有一个自动控制系统它可以唤醒我们在所有睡眠阶段当它感觉到紧急情况像孩子的哭声。

But the problem is that, in the modern world, our ancient innate wake-up call is constantly triggered by something that is non-life-threatening, like worrying before an exam or the unexpected sound of a car alarm.
但问题是，在现代世界，我们古老的觉醒电话经常被一些威胁生命的东西触发，比如在考试前担心或者汽车警报的意外声音。
Before the Industrial Revolution, which brought us alarm clocks and fixed work schedules, we could often counteract a sleep deficit by simply sleeping in.
工业革命给我们带来了闹钟和固定的工作时间表，在这场革命之前，我们往往可以通过睡觉来弥补睡眠不足。
That is no longer possible.
这已经不可能了。

paragraphs.brief: 事实上，缺乏睡眠与肥胖直接相关：没有足够的睡眠，胃和其他器官过度生产grelin，饥饿激素，导致我们食用更多。
sentences: The first segment of the brain that begins to fail when we don’t get enough sleep is the prefrontal cortex, the center of decision-making and problem-solving.
大脑中第一个在睡眠不足时开始失败的部分是前额皮层，决策和解决问题的中心。

Dr Chiara Cirelli, a neuroscientist in the U.S., suggests that, ‘Every cognitive function to some extent seems to be affected by sleep loss,’ and she comments that people are often more irritable, moody, and irrational.
美国的神经科学家奇拉拉·西雷利博士指出，“每个认知功能似乎都受到睡眠丧失的影响”，她评论说，人们往往更情绪化、情绪化和不理性。
For instance, sleep-deprived suspects held by the police will often confess to anything in exchange for rest.
例如，被警察拘留的睡眠不足的嫌疑人往往会招供，以换取休息。
Other research has also found that people who regularly sleep less than six hours a night have an elevated risk of developing depression, as well as other mental and physical illnesses.
其他研究还发现，每晚睡眠不足6小时的人，患抑郁症和其他精神和身体疾病的风险较高。
In fact, lack of sleep has been directly tied to obesity: without enough sleep, the stomach and other organs overproduce ghrelin, the hunger hormone, causing us to eat more.
事实上，缺乏睡眠与肥胖直接相关：没有足够的睡眠，胃和其他器官过度生产grelin，饥饿激素，导致我们食用更多。
However, proving a cause-and-effect relationship in this case is challenging because subjecting humans to the necessary experiments is unethical.
然而，在这种情况下证明因果关系具有挑战性，因为让人类接受必要的实验是不道德的。

paragraphs.brief: NREM的四个阶段的第一个阶段被称为睡眠的浅端，其特征是大脑活动有独特的常规模式，如电子脑图(EEEG)设备所示，该设备是测量电脉冲的机器。
sentences: NREM (Non-Rapid Eye Movement) makes up the first of two distinct and repetitive phases of a night’s sleep.
非狂野眼球运动是夜间睡眠两个截然不同和重复阶段的第一个阶段。
As we fall into NREM sleep, our brain stays active and begins an editing process—deciding which memories to keep and which ones to ignore.
当我们进入NREM睡眠期时，我们的大脑保持活跃，开始编辑过程——决定要保留哪些记忆和哪些记忆可以忽略。

The first of NREM’s four stages is called the shallow end of sleep and is characterized by a distinctive regular pattern of brain activity, as shown on an EEG (electroencephalogram) device—a machine that measures electrical impulses.
NREM的四个阶段的第一个阶段被称为睡眠的浅端，其特征是大脑活动有独特的常规模式，如电子脑图(EEEG)设备所示，该设备是测量电脉冲的机器。
In stage two, the EEG measures electric sparks that strike the cerebral cortex (grey matter covering the outer layer of the brain) in regular half-second intervals.
在第二阶段，EEG测量电火花，以正常的半秒间隔撞击大脑皮层(脑外层的灰物质)。
Researchers believe that this electrical activity helps the cortex preserve and store recently acquired information.
研究人员认为，这种电活动有助于皮层保存和储存最近获得的信息。
Stages three and four have been described as a deep, coma-like sleep that is as essential to our brain as food is to our body.
第三和第四阶段被描述为一种深沉的、昏迷的睡眠它对我们的大脑和食物一样重要
In stage three, big, rolling waves of brain activity as measured on an EEG are present less than half the time; in stage four, more than half the time.
在第三阶段，脑电图上测得的大型、滚动的脑活动波不到一半的时间；第四阶段超过一半的时间。
It’s in this deep sleep that our cells produce most growth hormone, which is needed throughout life to service bones and muscles.
正是在这种深沉的睡眠中我们的细胞产生最多的生长激素，这是整个生命中需要的来为骨骼和肌肉服务。

paragraphs.brief: REM(光眼运动)的睡眠最初被认为只是NREM睡眠阶段的变异，并不特别显著。
sentences: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep was at first believed to be only a variation of a stage in NREM sleep, and not particularly significant.
REM(光眼运动)的睡眠最初被认为只是NREM睡眠阶段的变异，并不特别显著。

However, once scientists documented the distinctive eye movements in REM, and found that virtually all dreaming takes place during this period, REM sleep was recognized as the second major phase of sleep.
然而，一旦科学家记录了REM中独特的眼睛运动，发现几乎所有梦都发生在这一时期，REM睡眠被认为是睡眠的第二个主要阶段。
Today, scientists believe that the content of our approximately two hours of dreams each night in REM sleep is important in the processing of new memories.
今天，科学家们认为，我们每天晚上在REM睡眠中做大约两个小时的梦的内容，对于处理新的记忆十分重要。
Some sleep theorists argue that REM sleep is when we are our most intelligent, insightful, creative, and free.
一些睡眠理论家认为，我们是最聪明、最有见地、最有创意和最自由的时候，是REM睡眠。
It’s when we truly come alive.
我们真正活着的时候。
‘REM sleep may be the thing that makes us the most human, both for what it does for the brain and body, and for the sheer experience of it,’ says Professor Michael Perlis.
迈克尔·佩利斯教授说，这是纯粹的体验：“REM 睡眠可能是我们最人性的东西不管是对大脑还是身体的影响。”

paragraphs.brief: 失去睡眠的问题不是很容易解决的，无论是用静脉注射还是用药。
sentences: The problem of sleep loss is not easily solved—whether by power naps or pharmaceuticals.
失去睡眠的问题不是很容易解决的，无论是用静脉注射还是用药。

Dr Jeffrey Ellenbogen, a sleep scientist at Johns Hopkins University in the U.S., argues, ‘It’s tempting to manipulate sleep with drugs or devices, but we don’t yet understand sleep enough to risk artificially manipulating the parts.’
Jeffrey Ellenbogen博士是美国约翰霍普金斯大学的睡眠科学家，认为“用毒品或器械操控睡眠很诱人，但我们还不能理解睡眠是否足以冒人为操纵器官的风险。”
Dr Ellenbogen and other experts argue against shortcuts, especially the notion that we can mostly do without sleep.
埃伦博根博士和其他专家反对捷径，特别是我们大多数可以不睡觉的观念。
In fact, Dr Steven Lockley, of Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Boston, suggests that sleep may be more essential to us than food.
事实上，波士顿布里加姆和妇女医院的史蒂文·洛克利博士认为，睡眠比食物更重要。

items.en: an example of how sleeplessness can influence a person accused of a crime
items.zh: 失眠如何影响被指控犯罪的人的实例
items.why: 明确说到“嫌疑人 (suspects)”在睡眠剥夺下更容易招供，正是被指控犯罪者受影响的“例子”。

items.en: a description of recordings of different types of brain activity during sleep
items.zh: 描述睡眠期间各类大脑活动的记录
items.why: 连续用EEG 刻画各阶段脑活动与波形差异，这是“记录不同脑活动类型的直接描述。

items.en: a description of how present-day society interrupts sleep
items.zh: 描述当今社会如何干扰睡眠
items.why: 当代的考试焦虑、汽车报警、闹钟与固定作息= 现代社会机制对睡眠的持续干扰。

items.en: information about the relationship between being overweight and sleep
items.zh: 超重与睡眠之间的关系信息
items.why: D段把缺觉与肥胖相联，解释睡眠不足时饥饿激素可能增多并促使人进食。

items.en: a suggestion that medication is an ineffective solution for sleeping problems
items.zh: 认为药物治疗是解决睡眠问题的一个无效办法
items.why: 直接否定“药片/捷径” 的有效性。后文还反对“可以基本不睡” 的想法。

items.en: a discovery that changed ideas about how sleep is understood
items.zh: 改变对睡眠理解的观念的发现
items.why: 这一发现把REM 从“无足轻重的NREM 变体” 提升为独立主要阶段，改变了原有认识。

items.en: examples of the life-threatening consequences of inadequate sleep
items.zh: 睡眠不足对生命造成威胁的实例
items.why: 夏令时调整使睡眠机会少一小时，随后心脏病发作和致命车祸增加，都是可能危及生命的后果。

items.en: Which TWO of these statements describe characteristics of NREM sleep?
items.zh: 其中哪两份陈述描述了NREM睡眠的特点？
correct: NREM sleep is important for maintaining brain function.
NREM睡眠对于保持大脑功能很重要。
Each stage of NREM sleep has a unique EEG pattern.
NREM睡眠的每个阶段都有独特的EEG模式。

items.en: Which TWO of these statements describe the characteristics of REM sleep?
items.zh: 其中哪两份陈述描述了REM睡眠的特点？
correct: REM sleep can be identified by an unusual physical feature.
REM睡眠可以用不寻常的物理特征来识别。
Some scientists consider REM sleep to be a source of human innovation.
有些科学家认为睡眠是人类创新的源泉。

items.en: According to the CDC, lack of sleep leads to ________, which is often a factor in car crashes.
items.zh: 据美国疾控中心介绍，缺乏睡眠会导致________，而这往往是车祸的诱因之一。
items.why: 回到对应内容“由此造成的疲劳导致每年发生100多万次汽车事故，并造成大量医疗错误”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The most common sleep disorder in the U.S. is ________.
items.zh: 美国最常见的睡眠障碍是________。

items.en: The brain responds to any type of ________ by activating a built-in alarm.
items.zh: 面对任何类型的________，大脑都会启动内置的警报机制。
items.why: “automatic override system =内置警报”,关键词即 emergency.

items.en: Researchers claim that routinely sleep-deprived people are more likely to be obese and suffer from illnesses like ________.
items.zh: 研究人员指出，经常睡眠不足的人更容易肥胖，也更容易患上________等疾病。
items.why: 空格要求“如…之类的 (like) ”的例子，文中点名 depression。

items.en: The processing of new memories is crucially linked to our ________ during sleep.
items.zh: 对新记忆的加工与我们睡眠时的________密切相关。
items.why: 回到对应内容“今天，科学家们认为，我们每天晚上在REM睡眠中做大约两个小时的梦的内容，对于处理新的记忆十分重要”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 当代的考试焦虑、汽车报警、闹钟与固定作息= 现代社会机制对睡眠的持续干扰。
“automatic override system =内置警报”,关键词即 emergency.
clauses: The brain has an automatic override system ….
“that can wake us in all stages of sleep when it perceives an emergency like the cry of a child”修饰前面的 system。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 system，再把修饰信息接回主句。
However, proving a cause-and-effect relationship in this case is challenging ….
连接词 because 引出“because subjecting humans to the necessary experiments is unethical”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
